title: Dragging a formula down makes every row point at a different rate

hook.body:
six hours cost more
than seven

payoff.headline:
LOCK IT
OR IT
WALKS
payoff.sub: If it shouldn't move, put dollar signs on it.

script.vo: You typed it once, dragged it down, and six hours cost more than seven.
Hours in A, labor cost in B.
script.caption:
Hours in A.
Labor cost in B.

script.vo: The rates sit in a small table underneath. Standard, overtime, mileage.
script.caption:
Rate table underneath.
Standard, overtime, mileage.

script.vo: Row two was hours times the standard rate. Then the drag hit row three.
script.caption: Then the drag hit row 3.

script.vo: Six hours at the overtime rate.
script.caption:
Six hours at the
overtime rate.

script.vo: The reference moved with the formula, one row down.
script.caption:
The reference moved
with the formula.

script.vo: The hours should move. The rate shouldn't. So lock the rate cell with dollar signs.
script.caption:
Lock the rate cell
with *$*.

script.vo: Dollar signs on the row and the column.
script.caption: Row and column, both.

script.vo: 252.00. Standard rate, like it should have been.
script.caption: 252.00. Standard rate.

script.vo: F4 cycles the dollar signs. Drag it now and every row still reads B8.
script.caption: Every row holds B8.

script.vo: Anything that shouldn't move needs dollar signs.

post.title: Dragged the formula down and every row grabbed a different rate
post.description:
formula changes cells when i drag it down in excel
A reference without dollar signs shifts one row for every row you drag, so lock the cell you always want it to read. Save this one.
